title: Cluster secrets scoped to a project stop serving Applications and ApplicationSets of other projects

detection.reason: a Secret's `project` KEY is collected but its value is not, and the Applications that use the cluster are not related to it in the inventory

quote: What this means is that if you have a cluster secret scoped to `project-a`, an application scoped to `project-b` can no longer make use of the secret. If you have a cluster secret that's intended to be used by applications in multiple projects, you need to **unset** the `project` field.
remediation: For each cluster secret carrying a `project`, confirm only Applications of that project (and no ApplicationSet git generator) target it; unset `project` on secrets meant to be shared before upgrading.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n argocd get secret -l argocd.argoproj.io/secret-type=cluster -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.data.project != null) | .metadata.name + " project=" + (.data.project | @base64d)' # secrets printed are project-scoped — Applications of other projects lose them at 2.12

title: `redis` and `haproxy` images move from Docker Hub to ECR

detection.reason: whether your registry mirror, allow-list or image-signature policy admits public.ecr.aws is not something the cluster inventory records

quote: As part of the upgrade, the image registry for `redis` and `haproxy` was changed from DockerHub to ECR.
remediation: Add `public.ecr.aws` to your registry allow-list / mirror / Cosign policy, or override the redis and haproxy image repositories in your overlay, before applying the 2.12 manifests.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n argocd get deploy,sts -o json | jq -r '.items[].spec.template.spec.containers[] | select(.image | test("redis|haproxy")) | .image' | sort -u # images printed are what the 2.12 manifests re-point to public.ecr.aws

title: ApplicationSet label selectors become atomic — two field managers can no longer share one

detection.reason: field managers of an ApplicationSet's selector fields are not collected

quote: If you are using server-side apply with multiple field managers to manage a single `selector` or `labelSelector` field in an ApplicationSet, that field management must be changed to be atomic starting with 2.12.
remediation: Where more than one tool server-side-applies parts of an ApplicationSet's generator selectors, make one of them own the whole selector (`matchLabels` and `matchExpressions` together) before upgrading the CRD.
verifyCommand: kubectl get applicationsets -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.managedFields[1] != null) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name + ": " + ([.metadata.managedFields[].manager] | unique | join(","))' # ApplicationSets printed have several field managers — check whether two of them touch one selector

title: Built-in health checks added for 18 resource kinds — Applications that deploy them can turn Degraded or Progressing

detection.reason: objects of these custom resource kinds, and their current health, are not collected; the hint names the installed CRDs whose group and kind are on the list (group and kind are matched separately, so a CRD pairing a listed group with another listed group's kind is named too)

quote: * core.humio.com/HumioAction * core.humio.com/HumioAlert * core.humio.com/HumioCluster * core.humio.com/HumioIngestToken * core.humio.com/HumioParser * core.humio.com/HumioRepository * core.humio.com/HumioView * k8s.mariadb.com/Backup * k8s.mariadb.com/Database * k8s.mariadb.com/Grant * k8s.mariadb.com/MariaDB * k8s.mariadb.com/SqlJob * k8s.mariadb.com/User * kafka.strimzi.io/KafkaBridge * kafka.strimzi.io/KafkaConnector * keda.sh/ScaledObject * openfaas.com/Function * camel.apache.org/Integration
remediation: Objects of these kinds start counting toward their Application's health at this version: one the new check reads as Degraded or Progressing turns its Application Degraded or Progressing and holds later sync waves. Check the status of these objects in the Applications that deploy them before upgrading, or override a kind with `resource.customizations.health.<group>_<Kind>` in argocd-cm.
verifyCommand: kubectl get crd -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(IN(.spec.group + "/" + .spec.names.kind; "core.humio.com/HumioAction", "core.humio.com/HumioAlert", "core.humio.com/HumioCluster", "core.humio.com/HumioIngestToken", "core.humio.com/HumioParser", "core.humio.com/HumioRepository", "core.humio.com/HumioView", "k8s.mariadb.com/Backup", "k8s.mariadb.com/Database", "k8s.mariadb.com/Grant", "k8s.mariadb.com/MariaDB", "k8s.mariadb.com/SqlJob", "k8s.mariadb.com/User", "kafka.strimzi.io/KafkaBridge", "kafka.strimzi.io/KafkaConnector", "keda.sh/ScaledObject", "openfaas.com/Function", "camel.apache.org/Integration")) | .metadata.name' # CRDs printed gain an Argo CD health check at 2.12 — check the status of their objects in your Applications
